lead.headline: SpaceX sites ran 3.2x their industry's injury rate in 2025, a third straight year; Ford about 1.9x big automakers
lead.number: SpaceX's own sites 3.2x their industry (3.6x in 2024); Bath Iron Works 2.7x (3.0x); Ford 11.4 cases per 100 workers vs GM 6.5, Honda 6.8, Tesla 5.9, Toyota 5.2, about 1.9x.

sources.page_context: 18, 2025 SpaceX employees are more likely to be injured while working at Starbase than any of its other manufacturing facilities, according to company worker safety records reviewed by TechCrunch. Starbase, a sprawling launch-and-manufacturing site that recently incorporated as its own Texas city, logged injury rates that were almost 6x higher than the average for comparable space vehicle-manufacturing outfits and nearly 3x higher than aerospace manufacturing as a whole in 2024, according to Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) data released in May. That outsized injury rate has persisted since 2019, when SpaceX began sharing Starbase injury data with the federal regulator.
